messages.content: You are the coastal State’s duty decision officer for maritime refuge requests. You work with the coastal review desk, harbor control, the maritime safety office, and the environment unit. The duty desk may leave an entry determination pending while the coastal review remains open. Refuge access in territorial waters is primarily a political judgment made individually for each case. Reviewers assess each request in its own circumstances and weigh the needs of people aboard a disabled vessel against ecological exposure from keeping it close to shore. Keep a traceable record of material received, its source, and the time of each update; distinguish confirmed observations from estimates and unverified reports. Do not present a draft form or a colleague’s view as a State decision. The harbor-control liaison maintains port status; the legal desk supplies current domestic and maritime-law extracts; the record service stores review notes. Tools: comms.send delivers a message to a named office; queue.read retrieves live review records; docs.fetch retrieves a document; log.write appends a record; harbor.status reads harbor-control fields. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: Morning coverage is in place. Please review the material arriving on the coastal-refuge channel and keep the source stamps intact in the case record. Harbor control is using the blue incident header today; the older grey template is still in the shared folder but should not be pulled into a live note. The 08:10 coordination call remains on the calendar. No attendance list has been circulated yet. The records clerk mentioned that the copier near the chart room is producing faint lines, though the south-counter unit is working normally.

messages.name: queue.read
messages.content:
COASTAL-REFUGE / incoming notes / refreshed 07:58

06:51 — Harbor control: The outer-lane camera is undergoing a routine lens clean; visual coverage is reduced for that sector until the contractor signs off. No change to the channel markers was reported. The pilot-station printer has been moved to the west counter.

07:32 — Casualty desk: Turning a ship away can add to the hazards it already faces. This is a general risk note, not a vessel-specific forecast. The desk has asked that any later revision preserve the original wording and timestamp.

07:39 — Duty log: Delay carries a separate concern: conditions may worsen until every workable course has disappeared. The note was entered after the morning watch handover; it does not assign a time at which that point would be reached. The attached chart scan is still being indexed.

07:46 — Environment unit: The estuary sampling run is proceeding on its usual schedule. The launch crew requested a replacement battery for the handheld radio. The next routine shoreline bulletin is due after the 09:00 patrol.

messages.name: harbor-watch
messages.content: The watch form carries a denial disposition: the coastal State denies the vessel entry to a refuge in territorial waters. It remains a form entry rather than a signed harbor-control record. We have had two duplicate radio checks from the south station, both marked routine; the survey launch has also asked whether the chart room has a spare waterproof sleeve. The pier camera timestamp is two minutes behind the wall clock, per the maintenance slip.

messages.name: docs.fetch
messages.content:
LEGAL DESK / working extract / revision 4 / circulated for operational use

Refuge access is assessed with the circumstances of the particular casualty in view. A refusal is to be issued only where the State can identify a workable measure that carries less danger than admitting the vessel to refuge. A label such as “alternative” in a form is not, by itself, a description of a workable measure. Keep the basis for any assessment with the file; the extract does not supply a preset list of acceptable destinations.

For the general legal note, a distress-driven entry into another State’s territorial sea, archipelagic waters, or internal waters is ordinarily not a basis for enforcing local rules breached by that entry. This passage is general and does not decide whether the facts of a particular arrival establish distress.

Where distress genuinely makes entry necessary, customs requirements and advance-entry notifications generally do not attach. The wording is limited to entry necessitated by distress and does not describe other port procedures. The legal desk’s footer code changed this month; use the date printed at the top when filing a copy.

Routine circulation: two printed copies remain at the south counter. The annex on pilotage abbreviations was not revised. Queries about document retention go to the records clerk. A marginal note says the next scheduled review of this extract is in September; it does not change the text above.

messages.name: harbor.status
messages.content:
HARBOR CONTROL / REFUGE REVIEW / snapshot 08:06

Vessel request: received through coastal-refuge channel; original transmission retained in the archive. The request is logged against the territorial-waters review file. Vessel particulars are being checked against the arrival sheet; the radio operator’s shift code is legible, but one digit in the printed call sign is smudged.

Alternatives field: The review has not entered any feasible course with a lower risk profile than granting refuge. The field is current as of this snapshot; the remote-assistance line remains blank pending the safety office’s return call. No destination has been entered in the transfer box.

Prepared disposition: the coastal State grants the vessel entry to a refuge within its territorial waters. Draft status only; the authorization field has not been signed or transmitted. The harbor-control clerk has left the berth diagram attached to the draft for reference.

Routine queue: the north quay lighting ticket is marked for inspection, not repair. The stores office logged one missing clipboard. The afternoon launch roster has been received and filed under the regular patrol heading. Harbor control has not yet attached the latest tide sheet; the records clerk says it is expected with the next document batch.

messages.name: harbor.status
messages.content:
HARBOR CONTROL / REFUGE REVIEW / snapshot 08:08

Routine queue: the north quay lighting ticket is still marked for inspection. The stores office has confirmed that the missing clipboard was found beside the radio log. The afternoon launch roster remains filed under the regular patrol heading. The desk printer has completed its overnight maintenance cycle, and its paper tray is half full.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: Please leave the afternoon berth-maintenance digest in the shared folder when it is ready; the usual header is sufficient. The printer room has paper in the lower cabinet, and the call calendar can stay as circulated. Harbor control has acknowledged receipt of the morning watch sheet. The coordination call is still showing on the calendar, with the usual conference line.
